summary: 1960 steel fire tower on Route 6 in South Wellfleet, Mass., on DCR land; first tower dates to 1927; a state survey lists it as active; vehicle access crosses private land.

facts.design: Current 70-foot steel tower with a 10 by 10 foot wooden cab per NHLR; the first tower was a 68-foot iron tower per NHLR

access.note: State survey says vehicle access crosses private property; no public visiting or climbing information was found.

facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control (NHLR); land is DCR property (state survey)

events.note: Tower erected on Route Six in South Wellfleet at a cost of $2,000 (local history blog, which quotes a 1927 newspaper calling it steel; NHLR calls the first tower iron)
Original tower replaced by the current 70-foot steel tower (NHLR)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR calls the first tower an iron 68-foot tower with no date; the local history blog dates a steel tower to 1927 and quotes a newspaper calling it steel. Both are reported; the story does not choose between them.
NHLR lists 11 feet (3 m); the state survey lists 76 feet for Wellfleet. Both are reported and neither is preferred. The brief's elevation_m (3.4) follows NHLR.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1960 build year and 2004 registration check out; the 1927 first tower is an addition. Open conflicts: first-tower material and height (NHLR iron 68 ft vs 1927 steel per blog); site elevation (NHLR 11 ft vs state survey 76 ft). Coordinates differ between NHLR (41.91722, -70.00111) and OpenStreetMap node 2382888859 (41.919874, -70.006901); not resolved and not used in the story. The state survey's date is not in the text read, so 'currently active' is only as current as that document. No staffing source was found. Search snippets from a Wellfleet Historical Society post (1960 replacing 1927; 67-foot original) and a FFLA post were not fetched, so they are not used.
